world.bio: I teach Year 3 in Brunswick and run the school veggie garden, where the kids have named every tomato plant. This term the tomatoes are called Gandalf, Beyoncé and Kevin. I play wing defence in a Thursday night netball team and am training for my first half marathon, losing toenails in the process. I inherited my grandmother's 1950s Singer sewing machine and the bobbin mechanism jams on every second stitch.
skills_assets: Eleven years teaching primary school, six at Brunswick Primary
Running a school veggie garden with about forty kids across three year levels
A Thursday netball team that is somehow top of the ladder
A 1950s Singer treadle machine from my grandmother, inherited in March, currently jammed
Beginner-level sewing and a half-finished set of cushion covers
A partner, Tom, who is tiling the bathroom himself and it is going badly

projects.name: School veggie garden
projects.text: The garden has twelve raised beds, built in 2022 with a small grant. Year 3 handles tomatoes, Year 4 does herbs, Year 5 manages the compost. We are in the spring planting window: peas, broad beans, lettuce. A parent donated a worm farm, which the kids love and I have to remind them not to take home. Funding runs out in December and I need to write the next application by mid-October.

projects.name: Grandma's Singer
projects.text: I inherited Nana's treadle Singer in March when she moved into aged care. It sits in the corner of the lounge with a doily on it. The bobbin case jams on every second stitch, and I cannot work out whether it is dust, a bent part or my own incompetence. I have watched four YouTube videos and taken it apart once and put it back with two screws left over. I want to make a patchwork quilt on it for my sister's baby, due in February.

projects.name: Netball 队服征集
projects.text: 队里要换新队服，队长让我负责设计。我画了三版草图，最后选了深蓝配亮橙，肩膀上有一道闪电。队友说像是体育用品店的广告，我说那你来画。她们立刻闭嘴。

notes.text: Gandalf the tomato is three feet tall and one of my Year 3s told me it needs a staff. I said what kind of staff. She said 'a wizard one'. Found a bamboo stake and let her tie a bit of ribbon to the top. Gandalf now has a staff. Best use of fourteen minutes this week.

Half marathon training: 14 km, lost another toenail. Tom says I should stop. I said I will stop when I finish. He said that is not how stopping works. Went to the physio, who said my right glute is a lazy tyrant. Prescribed clams and bridges and a sad face.

Tom has been tiling the bathroom for nine weekends. The grout looks like cake icing smeared by a toddler. I said it's very rustic. He said it's meant to be modern. We stood there silently in front of the shower wall for a while, two adults admiring a disaster.

Netball Thursday: won by eleven. I intercepted three balls and shouted so loudly that the umpire asked me to calm down. Played wing defence like a menace. The other team's centre looked at me like I had eaten her sandwich.

Took the Singer apart again with the YouTube lady. Found a small bit of old thread wound round the shuttle hook. Cleaned it out with a toothpick. Put it back. The bobbin jammed on the very first stitch. Nana would have laughed. She used to say a machine is like a person: it only works if you listen.

Visited Nana in aged care. She asked if I was using the Singer. I said yes, a bit. She smiled and said 'don't lie'. I admitted it was jammed. She said, 'Your grandfather used to oil it with a feather.' I have no idea what that means, and she could not explain. She asked about the tomatoes and I told her their names.
Staff meeting: the principal announced a new literacy framework. I took notes on the back of a seed packet. Realised halfway through that my notes were mostly about which seeds to plant in November.

Grant application is due in two weeks. I have written 400 words and deleted 350. 'Our garden fosters growth' is not a sentence, it is a mug slogan. Need to find something concrete: numbers of kids, vegetables harvested, a parent testimonial.

Long run along the Merri Creek, 16 km, ended with a cold shower and a pie. Tom had finished the first row of tiles at an angle and called it 'organic'. I laughed so hard I had to sit on the edge of the bath. Which, to be fair, had tile adhesive on it.

messages.text:
Linh: Are you still on for making the quilt?
Me: In theory.
Linh: In theory?
Me: The machine is jammed.
Linh: I can buy a baby blanket.
Me: Nope, I'm doing it. Just need a miracle.

Tom: Grout dries in four hours. Don't use the shower until tomorrow.
Me: Where do I wash?
Tom: The sink.
Me: I'm going to my sister's.
Tom: Don't be dramatic.

Sam: Can we do a working bee next Saturday? I'll bring the wheelbarrow.
Me: Yes please! The beans need staking.
Sam: And I've got a bag of blood and bone.
Me: You're my favourite parent.

Jo: You coming Thursday?
Me: Absolutely.
Jo: Even with the toenails?
Me: Even with the toenails.

relations.about: My grandmother, 91, in aged care in Preston. Sharp as a pin, forgetful about the present.
Partner, a project manager who is not a tiler.

constraints: Weekdays are school hours, so weekends only
Do not want to spend more than a few hundred dollars on the machine
Cannot attend events on Thursday nights
The garden application must go in by mid-October
sensitive: Afraid I won't finish the half marathon
